articles.title: Meta Shares Plunge as AI Investments Raise Spending Outlook
articles.text: Meta Platforms Inc. shares slid after the company raised its spending outlook for the year, reigniting fears that the historic levels of investment it's making to build artificial intelligence models won't pay off. The social-media giant projected full-year capital expenditures between $125 billion and $145 billion, far exceeding analysts' estimates and marking a roughly 7.4% increase from what the company had previously projected.

articles.title: Meta Q1 Review: The Market Has Lost Its Mind
articles.text: Meta Platforms, Inc. delivered strong Q1 results, beating consensus on both revenue and EPS. META's EPS exceeded analyst expectations by over 55%, yet shares declined 7% post-earnings. I view the market's negative reaction as a significant overreaction, creating a compelling buying opportunity.

articles.title: Meta Platforms (META) Q1 Earnings and Revenues Surpass Estimates
articles.text: Meta Platforms (META) came out with quarterly earnings of $7.31 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $6.71 per share. This compares to earnings of $6.43 per share a year ago.

articles.title: Meta's Earnings Paradox: A Brilliant Quarter The Market Chose To Punish
articles.text: Meta Platforms, Inc. delivered exceptional Q1 results, with revenue of $56.31B and adjusted EPS of $7.31, both beating consensus estimates. Despite strong fundamentals, META shares declined due to a significant upward revision in 2026 capex guidance to $125–$145B, raising concerns about capital intensity. AI-driven improvements boosted average ad price by 12% YoY, signaling early monetization benefits and reinforcing META's competitive moat in digital advertising.

articles.title: Meta Q1: Thanks For The Dip, I'm Buying More
articles.text: Meta Platforms, Inc. delivered robust Q1 results with 33% YoY revenue growth, strong ad momentum, and resilient user engagement despite mature platforms. EPS was inflated by a one-time $8B tax benefit; underlying performance remains solid, driven by 19% ad impression and 12% price-per-ad growth. CapEx guidance for 2026 increased to $125–$145B, raising near-term FCF concerns but supporting long-term AI and platform investments.

articles.text: Meta Platforms is getting thrifty in the face of the memory crunch.
